execSummary: Piedmont Precision Components seeks a $5.0M equipment term loan to fund three Mazak INTEGREX multi-tasking CNC machines, alongside a $2.5M increase & renewal of its existing $5.0M working-capital revolver (to $7.5M). The borrower is a 26-year aerospace/defense precision machinist (AS9100D / ISO 13485) with a diversified blue-chip customer base and a multi-year contracted backlog. FY2025 revenue reached $64.5M (+7.6% YoY), but adjusted EBITDA margin softened to 8.1% ($5.2M) on elevated labor and new-program qualification costs, lifting leverage to 3.85x (~4.8x pro forma). Liquidity ($8.2M) and DSC (1.42x) remain inside covenant, and the unlimited guaranty of principal Margaret Holloway provides additional support. Recommended for approval at a 5 — Pass/Watch risk rating, with close monitoring of the margin trend.
requestDetails:
Purpose. $5.0M new-money equipment term loan (7-year, monthly amortization) to acquire three Mazak INTEGREX i-450 multi-tasking CNC centers supporting a newly awarded defense program. Concurrently, the existing $5.0M working-capital revolver is increased by $2.5M to $7.5M and renewed for 364 days.

Sources & Uses. Uses: $5.0M equipment + $2.5M incremental working capital = $7.5M new money. Sources: $5.0M bank equipment term loan + $2.5M revolver increase.
borrowerDescription: Piedmont Precision Components, Inc., founded in 1998 and headquartered in Greensboro, NC, is a privately held precision-machining manufacturer. From a single ~110,000 sq ft campus (182 employees; AS9100D / ISO 13485 certified) it machines high-tolerance, build-to-print components for aerospace, defense, and medical-device OEMs. Wholly owned by founder-CEO Margaret Holloway (full guaranty); a client of the bank since 2009.
strengthsRisks:
Strengths. AS9100D / ISO 13485 certifications create high switching costs; multi-year contracted backlog; tangible CNC-equipment collateral; full guaranty of the principal.

Risks & mitigants. FY2025 margin compression (8.1%, from ~11%) lifted leverage to 3.85x — mitigated by contracted price escalators and backlog conversion; customer concentration is offset by long program lifecycles and growing medical diversification; equipment-purchase risk is limited by the established Mazak platform.
managementOwnership: Margaret Holloway (founder, President & CEO; 100% owner) leads a stable senior team averaging 12+ years of tenure. No management changes occurred during the review period. Ms. Holloway provides an unlimited personal guaranty of the facilities.
financialCommentary: FY2025 revenue of $64.5M grew +7.6% year-over-year, but profitability softened: gross margin compressed to 21.8% and adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 8.1% ($5.2M, from ~9.7% in FY2024) on elevated direct labor, training, and first-article qualification costs ahead of full-rate production. Total funded debt of $20.1M (pro forma $25.1M including the $5.0M equipment loan) puts leverage at 3.85x EBITDA (~4.8x pro forma) — elevated for the rating but supported by tangible collateral and a contracted backlog.
financialFutureOutlook: Management projects EBITDA-margin recovery in FY2026 as the new medical-device program reaches full-rate production and qualification spend rolls off, supported by contracted price escalators and backlog conversion already underway. The margin trajectory remains the key monitoring item into 2026 — see Sensitivity Analysis below for the downside case.
covenantConditions: The proposed facilities carry four financial covenants, tested quarterly (Minimum Liquidity monthly): Minimum Debt Service Coverage (≥1.25x), Maximum Debt-to-Worth (≤3.00x), Minimum Liquidity (≥$5.0M), and Maximum Annual CapEx (≤$7.5M). All four are in compliance as of the most recent test date, with the thinnest cushion on debt-service coverage (1.42x actual vs. the 1.25x floor) — the covenant most exposed to the margin-compression trend discussed in the Financial Analysis section.
conditionsMonitoring: Conditions & Monitoring. Quarterly financial reporting with covenant compliance certificate; annual field exam of working-capital collateral; first-lien UCC on the financed equipment. Watch item: FY2025 EBITDA-margin recovery toward management plan in FY2026; revisit the risk rating if margin softening continues beyond Q2-2026.
riskRatingRationale: The proposed 5 — Pass/Watch rating reflects FY2025 EBITDA-margin compression (8.1%, from ~11% in FY2023) and pro forma leverage of ~4.8x, offset by tangible collateral coverage (112%–185%), a contracted multi-year backlog, and the principal's unlimited guaranty. The rating holds at the current level rather than downgrading because covenant headroom remains intact (DSC 1.42x vs. 1.25x) and management's FY2026 margin-recovery plan is supported by qualification-cost roll-off already underway. It does not improve because the margin trend has not yet turned and pro forma leverage sits above the peer median for the segment.
riskMitigantsNarrative: The principal risks in this credit — margin compression, customer concentration, key-man dependence on the principal, and leverage above the peer median — are each addressed by an identifiable mitigant carried elsewhere in this memo (collateral coverage, backlog conversion, the personal guaranty, and covenant headroom). None is assessed as elevating the proposed risk rating on its own; collectively they support quarterly monitoring rather than a rating change.
recommendation: Recommendation. Approve the $5.0M equipment term loan and the $2.5M increase & renewal of the working-capital revolver (to $7.5M) at a 5 — Pass/Watch risk rating. The credit is supported by tangible collateral, a contracted backlog, the principal's guaranty, and covenant headroom (DSC 1.42x vs 1.25x; liquidity $8.2M vs $5.0M), tempered by softening margins and elevated pro forma leverage.
guarantorProfile: Margaret Holloway provides an unlimited continuing guaranty of the Piedmont facilities. As founder and sole shareholder, her interests are fully aligned with the borrower. A current personal financial statement is on file; updated PFS and tax returns are a standard reporting condition.
globalCashFlow: On a combined basis, borrower operating cash flow plus guarantor liquidity covers pro forma fixed charges. Global debt-service coverage is supported primarily at the operating-company level, with the guaranty providing secondary support. A formal global cash-flow model will be maintained in AFS once the connector lands.
collateralBlanket: The working-capital line is secured by a first-priority blanket lien on all business assets, including accounts receivable and inventory, supported by a borrowing-base certificate and periodic field exams.
collateralEquipment: The equipment term loan is secured by a first-priority purchase-money security interest in the three financed Mazak INTEGREX CNC machines, plus the borrower's existing late-model machine tools. Orderly-liquidation coverage is supported by the active secondary market for Mazak multi-tasking equipment.
ews_summary: No active Early Warning Signals. Account-monitoring triggers — overdraft activity, covenant proximity, rapid line drawdown, and NSF events — are clear over the trailing twelve months. The EBITDA-margin compression noted in the financial analysis is carried as a watch item, not an EWS trigger.
entity_verification: Piedmont Precision Components, Inc. is verified as active and in good standing with the North Carolina Secretary of State (registered since 1998). No pending administrative dissolution or adverse status flags.
internet_search: Public-web and trade-press review surfaced no adverse media, litigation, regulatory action, or reputational concerns. Coverage is limited to routine industry and contract-award items consistent with the borrower's aerospace and defense customer base.
lexisnexis: LexisNexis returned no material liens, judgments, bankruptcies, or UCC filings outside the existing bank position. No adverse public records on the borrower or the guarantor.
credit_bureau: The commercial credit profile is satisfactory: no delinquencies, collections, or derogatory tradelines reported. Payment behavior on existing bank facilities is current, with zero 30-plus-day events in the trailing twelve months.
sbfe: Small Business Financial Exchange data corroborates a clean trade-payment history across reporting lenders, consistent with the AFS servicing record.
leading_indicators_commentary: Collectively the leading indicators support the proposed action: clean public records, satisfactory bureau and SBFE data, verified entity standing, and no adverse media. The single forward-looking watch item remains the margin trajectory, addressed in the financial analysis and sensitivity sections.
industryChanges: Demand drivers. Aerospace & defense precision machining benefits from a sustained U.S. defense-budget cycle and a multi-year commercial-aerospace build-rate recovery; long program lifecycles and AS9100D/ISO 13485 qualification barriers favor incumbent, certified suppliers like the borrower. Headwinds. Skilled-machinist labor scarcity and input-cost inflation continue to pressure margins sector-wide — consistent with the EBITDA-margin compression observed in the borrower's FY2025 results — while new-program qualification spend front-loads cost ahead of full-rate production revenue. On balance the sector outlook is stable-to-improving, with the borrower positioned in a defensible, certification-gated niche.
spreadingReadDollars: Top-line growth is intact — revenue compounded to $64.5M in FY2025 (+7.6% YoY) — but the absolute-dollar view understates the profitability story; switch to the margin % view to see the EBITDA-margin compression.
spreadingReadMargin: The margin lens surfaces the core finding the dollar view hides: gross margin compressed and EBITDA margin fell to 8.1% in FY2025 (from ~9.7% in FY2024 and ~11% in FY2023) on labor inflation and new-program qualification cost — the basis for the 5 — Pass/Watch rating and the Q2-2026 margin-recovery monitoring trigger.
borrowerSegments:
• Aerospace & Defense (~65%) — titanium and nickel-alloy components for defense primes and tier-1 aerospace suppliers, on multi-year build-to-print programs.
  • Medical Device (~20%) — ISO 13485 surgical-instrument and implantable components; the fastest-growing segment.
  • Industrial & Energy (~15%) — turbine, hydraulic, and fluid-control components for industrial OEMs.
borrowerGeography: Operations are consolidated at the Greensboro, NC campus; the customer base is concentrated in the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic, with aerospace and medical accounts expanding into the Northeast and Midwest.
borrowerCustomers: Tier-1 aerospace and defense OEMs and their sub-tier suppliers are the largest concentration. The top five customers are ~40% of revenue, all aerospace/defense — mitigated by long program lifecycles, switching costs, and growing medical-device diversification.
borrowerChanges:
Material developments flagged since the prior credit review:

  • New end market — medical device. An ISO 13485 cell grew the segment to ~20% of revenue (from ~8%) — the first diversification beyond aerospace/defense, and the main driver of the temporary FY2025 margin compression (8.1%, from ~11%).
  • Capacity investment (this request). $5.0M for three Mazak INTEGREX CNC machines — ~30% more 5-axis capacity, in-sourcing previously subcontracted work.
  • Backlog & revolver use. Growing backlog has lifted working-capital needs, supporting the $2.5M revolver increase (to $7.5M).
